about: Authored by the course team in the exact shape of Anthropic Messages API replies (content blocks and stop_reason). It is not captured model output. Replaying it tests the harness: the loop, the dispatcher, the permission layer and the stopping rule. The turns play in order whatever the tools return, so this says nothing about how a real model behaves.
task:
Goal:     Make the reservation API refuse an attendee name made only of spaces
          (HTTP 422), the same way it already refuses an empty name.
Context:  AfterHours, a FastAPI + SQLite app. AGENTS.md has the commands and rules.
          The web page trims names; the API does not, so "   " is accepted today.
Limits:   Change only files in app/ and tests/. Do not weaken or delete any test.
Deliver:  A test that fails before your fix, the smallest fix, and the full test output.
Stop:     When every test passes. Or after 12 steps.
Cost cap: 60,000 tokens for the whole run.

content.text: I'll start with the layout of the project.
The request model is in app/main.py and the existing name test is in tests/test_basics.py. Reading both.
`attendee` has min_length=1, and a space counts as a character, so "   " passes. Writing a test that shows the problem first.

input.content:
from .conftest import event_by_title

ESCAPE_ROOM = "Escape Room: The Locked Lab"   # seeded with 39 of 40 places taken


def test_a_name_of_only_spaces_is_refused(client):
    event = event_by_title(client, ESCAPE_ROOM)
    res = client.post(f"/api/events/{event['id']}/reservations", json={"attendee": "   "})
    assert res.status_code == 422


def test_a_name_with_a_space_inside_is_accepted(client):
    event = event_by_title(client, ESCAPE_ROOM)
    res = client.post(f"/api/events/{event['id']}/reservations", json={"attendee": "Maya Chen"})
    assert res.status_code == 201

content.text: The spaces-only test fails (201 instead of 422), as expected. Smallest fix: the field also needs at least one non-space character.

Done.

- app/main.py: `attendee` now also needs at least one non-space character (`pattern=r"\S"`), so a name made only of spaces gets HTTP 422.
- tests/test_names.py: two new tests (spaces only gives 422; "Maya Chen" gives 201).

Evidence: `python -m pytest -q` gives 10 passed. The new test failed before the fix and passes after it.
